notes.title: MateEngine 1.8.7 - The Aromantic Update
notes.content: [h2]This update focuses on small tweaks and improvements for custom VRM and ME models.[/h2][p][/p][p][b]Window / Taskbar Sitting[/b][/p][p]You might have noticed that some models could slightly "float" above or "sink" into the taskbar or windows due to their unique bone sizes. We've added a new slider called **"Window Sitting Y Offset"**. With this slider, you can manually adjust your avatar’s vertical position to better match the window or taskbar when sitting.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Why is there a slider, and why doesn’t it work perfectly like in other apps?[/b][/p][p]  Every VRM model can have different bone lengths and proportions. Because of this, it’s impossible to automatically 100% align every model, especially those with non-standard proportions (such as many anime-style avatars). The new slider allows you to *fine-tune* the sitting height of your avatar for the best fit in every case.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Other Changes[/b][/p][p]Steam DLCs (such as the Steam Halo accessories) have been moved lower in the settings menu to make space for the new Y Offset slider.[/p][p][/p]

tags.feature: You might have noticed that some models could slightly "float" above or "sink" into the taskbar or windows due to their unique bone sizes. We've added a new slider called **"Window Sitting Y Offset"**. With this slider, you can manually adjust your avatar’s vertical position to better match the window or taskbar when sitting.
Steam DLCs (such as the Steam Halo accessories) have been moved lower in the settings menu to make space for the new Y Offset slider.

This should be much less frequent now).[/p][/*][*][p]Improved the Window / Taskbar Sitting feature for better compatibility with custom VRM models. Note: due to different bone lengths in every model, perfect compatibility is not possible.[/p][/*][*][p]Overall CPU usage improved.[/p][/*][*][p]Overall GPU usage improved.[/p][/*][*][p]The AI now tries to use less GPU power. Results may vary.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Window / Taskbar Sitting:[/h3][list][*][p]Added 6 new lay/sit positions.[/p][/*][*][p]Now a total of 7 sitting/laying positions are picked randomly each time you place the avatar on a window or the taskbar. notes.title: MateEngine 1.8.5 - The Lesbian Update
notes.content: [p]MateEngine 1.8.5[/p][p][/p][h2]AI Changes:[/h2][p]You can now use custom system prompts to give your AI its very own character! Before, you were forced to use "Zome" as your AI chat assistant, but this update changes that. To create a custom prompt, go to:[/p][p]AppData/LocalLow/Shinymoon/MateEngineX/[/p][p]Find the file "ZomeAI\\_prompt.txt" and enter your custom system prompt.[/p][p]If you don't see this file, you need to open the chat with the avatar at least once so the file is generated. After entering your custom system prompt, make sure to delete "ZomeAI.json" and "ZomeAI.cache" so the AI chatbot resets and uses your custom prompt. Also, make sure to restart MateEngine.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Fixes:[/p][p]* Fixed an issue where the Steam Halo was not reset correctly when using a custom avatar. Previously, after resetting the avatar with a Steam Halo, you had to toggle it on and off twice to reactivate the item. This now works as expected.[/p][p]* Fixed an issue where the avatar would remain frozen in a sit or lay position after placing it on a window or taskbar and then turning off the Window/Taskbar Sitting feature.[/p][p]* Fixed an issue where the avatar would continue sitting on a window after the window was made fullscreen. Now, the avatar will jump off automatically when you make a window fullscreen.[/p][p]* Fixed an issue where the avatar did not play any sound when the AI chat generated a message. Pixel-Speech should now work again.[/p]

notes.title: MateEngine 1.8.4 - Pride Update
notes.content:
[p]MateEngine 1.8.4 – Pride Update[/p][p]Version 1.8.4 is all about colors! Personally, I’ve always been a big fan of lights, glow, and different colors. I noticed it sometimes looked out of place when I had a dark synthwave or generally dark wallpaper on my PC, and the desktop pet’s color didn’t fit the wallpaper at all. This update changes everything![/p][p][/p][p]Ambient Lights:
Introducing ambient lights: Now you can add up to three dynamic lights to your scene! Each ambient light is fully customizable—intensity, color, and saturation—so you can perfectly match your desktop pet to your wallpaper or mood.[/p][p][/p][p]Global Light:
The global light (previously just a simple on/off toggle) now gets its own sliders for intensity, saturation, and color. It’s a simplified version of the Ambient Lights system, so even basic setups look great.[/p][p][/p][p]Custom Animation Mods (For Developers):
Developers can now use the MEManipulator and Unity’s AnimationOverrideController to swap MateEngine’s default animations with your own custom ones.[/p][p][/p][p]Languages:
The Alarm, Screen Saver, and Ambient Light features have been translated into all supported languages.[/p][p][/p][p]Internal Changes:
The Save/Load handler is now fully modular, more secure, and easier to read.[/p]

tags.feature: Introducing ambient lights: Now you can add up to three dynamic lights to your scene! Each ambient light is fully customizable—intensity, color, and saturation—so you can perfectly match your desktop pet to your wallpaper or mood.

The global light (previously just a simple on/off toggle) now gets its own sliders for intensity, saturation, and color. It’s a simplified version of the Ambient Lights system, so even basic setups look great.
Developers can now use the MEManipulator and Unity’s AnimationOverrideController to swap MateEngine’s default animations with your own custom ones.
The Alarm, Screen Saver, and Ambient Light features have been translated into all supported languages.

Other Changes:

* Fixed menu color issues where custom themes weren't applied everywhere
* Small fixes for BigScreen mode
* Minor performance improvements for optimized VRM models

notes.title: MateEngine 1.8.1
notes.content:
MateEngine 1.8.1 – Changelog

UI Changes:

* Fixed: Radial Menu icon colors now display correctly when using custom color themes.
* Remove buttons in the Model menu are now always red, regardless of your color scheme.
* Added a 3-second confirmation timer to the Remove button to prevent accidental model or Steam Workshop deletions.
* Fixed: AI chat bubbles now use your selected menu color.
* Radial Menu now live-refreshes buttons when switching states (for example, from Idle to Macaroon or Dance), preventing accidental access to disabled features.
* Improved: Radial Menu separator is now a slightly transparent white for a cleaner look.

Macaroon Changes:

* Macaroon can now only be toggled via the Radial Menu; the "Drag + Right Click" hotkey has been removed.

Performance Improvements:

* Improved RAM handling when switching models.
* Fixed a memory leak that could increase RAM usage from around 300 MB to over 3 GB after many model swaps.
* Unused textures, meshes, and controllers are now properly unloaded.
* Best results with well-optimized VRM0.X, VRM1.X, and .ME files.
* Cleanup may not work with broken or poorly structured models.

Note:
A small memory leak may still occur after frequent model switching, especially when using poorly exported or low-quality user models. This is outside my control. If you notice RAM usage increasing after many swaps, simply restart MateEngine or stick to a single model. Also, using many mods increases initial memory usage, so keep your library to 4–10 models for best performance.

notes.title: MateEngine 1.8.0-GM MAJOR UPDATE
notes.content:
MateEngine 1.8.0

Major Menu and UI Changes

* The AI Chat, Settings, and Clothes menus are now combined into a single Circle Menu. Right-click to open the Circle Menu and access all three features instead of using separate keybinds.
* The Settings menu automatically moves to the left if your pet is sitting on the right edge of the screen, making controls more accessible.
* Head pats and hand holding are disabled while the Circle Menu, Settings, or Clothes menus are open. This prevents overlapping and awkward UI interactions.

New Features

* Big Screen Mode (Beta): Open the new Radial menu and press the Face or Head icon to make your pet appear extra large on your screen. You can touch its hair and pet the head by holding the left mouse button. This is still a beta feature, so some VRM or physics limitations may apply. Future updates may add an alarm function and custom expressions. There are also plans for screensaver-style automatic activation after user inactivity.
* The AI Chat’s chat bubbles now use your main and radial menu colors for a consistent and modern look.

Behavior and Functional Improvements

* Taskbar and window sitting behavior is improved. When you scale the avatar, it tries to stay positioned on top of the window or taskbar. The results may vary depending on the VRM file's base size.
* You can no longer scale the mascot while dragging it. This prevents glitches and positioning errors.
* AI Chat movement is more natural. The chat bubble is attached to the pet’s upper body and swings based on the avatar’s movement.

AI and Performance Updates

* The AI model has been updated from Qwen 2.5 1.5b to the new Qwen 3.0 1.7b model. This version responds more naturally and cutely. It is not perfect (since it uses only 1.7 billion parameters), but it offers the best experience for most systems.
* Note: Local Chat AI uses about 3 to 5 GB of RAM when active and is CPU-intensive. A Ryzen 5 or Intel Core 5 from 2020 or newer is recommended for smooth AI chat.
* Code cleanups and lower memory usage: The app now uses less memory overall. At startup, Task Manager may show 350 to 500 MB with the default model, but after the first garbage collection (which runs every 15 minutes), usage drops to 150 to 300 MB. Memory usage may vary with different models.
* The FPS number now uses the correct size. Previously, it was larger than other text.
* The FPS number is now right-aligned for a cleaner appearance.
* The FPS slider now uses only whole numbers. This fixes the problem where setting it to 60 FPS could result in rendering at 59 or 61 FPS.
* Five new dances have been added: Hip-Hop, Salsa, Sexy, and Shuffle.
* The Can Dance menu is now merged into the main menu, helping to save screen space for settings.
* The Mod Menu is also merged into the main menu to reduce clutter.
* A "Back" button has been added to the Mod List, VRM Model List, and Can Dance menus, based on your feedback. This should make navigation much clearer.
* Chibi Mode is now accessible in the new Circle or Radial menu. You no longer have to hover over the feet to enable or disable it.
* Chibi Mode now uses the same particle effects as the head pat animation.

Important Information about the Radial Menu

* In some animation states, such as dancing, certain functions may not be available. This is intentional and not a bug. For example, the AI Chat button is unavailable while the mascot is dancing; you need to be idle to talk to your mascot. This prevents interruptions in different animation states. Most options are available when your pet is idle.

Clothes for Zome

* Zome now has three example clothes buttons, accessible from the Circle Menu.
* Only .ME files support clothes toggles. .VRM0.x and .VRM1.x do not support clothes toggles.
* You must set up clothes toggles yourself on your .ME model by following this guide:
  [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/wiki/MateSDK#meclothes](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/wiki/MateSDK#meclothes)

Other Changes

* Added complete Japanese translation.
* Added complete Traditional Chinese translation.
* Added complete Korean translation.
* Improved the overall font structure of the menu for better readability and consistency across languages. The menu should now look much cleaner.
* The Audio Settings icon is now aligned to the right side of the menu to prevent translated text from overlapping with the icon.
* Fixed an issue where the menu glow effect was being cut off by the app, which made the menu look odd.
* Fixed an issue where sliders in different menus had inconsistent color shades.
* Added 8K textures to the default model "Zome."

Two New Avatars Added

1. Aldina
   Author: Yorshka (also creator of Zome)
   Description: A cute, tiny anime witch girl featuring a unique mix of red, silver, and toxic green colors.
   Author’s Website: [https://yorshkasencho.booth.pm/](https://yorshkasencho.booth.pm/)

2. Lazuli
   Author: Elychiffon
   Description: Lazuli is a magical, adorable catgirl—perfect for all neko lovers! Includes a clothes toggle feature to easily switch clothes on or off.
   Author’s Website: [https://elychiffon.booth.pm/](https://elychiffon.booth.pm/)

Fixed and Requested Community Changes

* Issue 35: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/35](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/35)
* Issue 74: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/74](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/74)
* Issue 136 / 96: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/136](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/136)
* Issue 131: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/131](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/131)
* Issue 123: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/123](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/123)
* Issue 76: [https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/76](https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine/issues/76)

notes.title: MateEngine 1.7.8
notes.content:
Changelog 1.7.8

Changes:

* Added Taskbar Sitting: This feature activates when you enable the option "Window & Taskbar Sitting" in the options menu. Open the menu, scroll down, and toggle the setting to use it.
* Updated Macaroon Activation: You can now enable or disable the Macaroon by dragging the pet and pressing the right mouse button while dragging.
* The Macaroon now scales based on the avatar’s size, ensuring proper proportions.
* Avatars cannot snap to windows or the taskbar while sitting on the Macaroon.
* Reverted the hair and eye colors of Zome (default avatar) to the original design.
* Reduced memory usage for the default avatar (Zome).
* Steam Workshop Clean-up:

  * When unsubscribing from models via Steam, they will be deleted from the "Steam Workshop" folder upon app restart.
  * When unsubscribing inside MateEngine using the "Remove" button, the app will automatically unsubscribe from Steam and instantly remove the model from the folder.
* Added "IK Feet" toggle. It is enabled by default to give the mascot more realistic foot and leg movement. However, some models may appear more feminine and natural with IK Feet disabled. I suggest experimenting with different models to see what works best for your setup.
* Added missing translations for several UI elements.

Todo:

* Change dance after a few seconds/minutes automatically
* Add more sitting animations

notes.title: Patch for 1.7.2-4
notes.content:
[b][h2]MateEngine 1.7.2-4 PATCH 2[/h2][/b]

[b]Workshop Changes:[/b]

[list]
[*] Images over 700KB are now blocked during avatar upload.
[*] If your mascot image is larger than 700KB, a "FIX IMG" button will appear. You must click it and choose a new image to continue.
[*] The new image must be a 1:1 square, be a .PNG file, and be under 700KB.
[*] If your avatar does not have an image at all, the "FIX IMG" button will also appear. You must assign a valid image before uploading.
[/list]

[b]MateEngine Improvements:[/b]

[list]
[*] Scroll-to-Size now only works when the menu is closed, to prevent accidental size changes.
[*] Scrolling in the Settings Menu no longer changes the avatar size.
[*] UI scrolling is now smoother and no longer sticky.
[/list]

[i]Memory allocation performance has been improved.
Note: this does not guarantee lower RAM usage. RAM usage depends on your model.
Optimized avatars typically use 100 to 300MB of RAM.
Heavy avatars with large textures or high polygon counts will use significantly more.

notes.title: MateEngine 1.7.2 – Steam Workshop Update
notes.content:
[h1]MateEngine 1.7.2 – Steam Workshop Update[/h1]

This update introduces [b]official Steam Workshop support![/b]

You can now upload your own characters to the Workshop using [b].VRM[/b] or [b].ME[/b] files — and it's super easy!

[hr][/hr]

[h2]How to Upload .VRM / .ME Files[/h2]

[olist]
[*] Import your .VRM or .ME file into MateEngine as usual.
[*] Click on the [b]Models[/b] tab to access the updated character menu.
[*] Hold the [b]Upload[/b] button for 5 seconds on the character you want to upload.
[*] The file will be uploaded to the Steam Workshop! Once done, you can edit the Workshop page directly.
[/olist]

Note: This feature is currently experimental and in public beta for testing purposes!
There may be bugs or missing features.
If your avatar doesn't upload to Steam, it might be due to the avatar image being too large.
We recommend using a .png file under 600 KB in size for best results.
[b]

Important: You have to restart MateEngine once you download models![/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Before Uploading[/h2]

Make sure the following fields are filled out:

[list]
[*] [b]Name[/b]
[*] [b]Version[/b]
[*] [b]Author[/b]
[*] [b]Thumbnail image[/b]
[/list]

You can either embed an image in the VRM metadata (check the tutorials), or manually add one in the [b]Thumbnails[/b] folder.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Important Files & Folders[/h2]

[i]Location:[/i]  
[code]C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME\AppData\LocalLow\Shinymoon\MateEngineX[/code]

[list]
[*] [b]Steam Workshop[/b] – Contains downloaded Workshop files.
[*] [b]Thumbnails[/b] – Add or replace model preview images here.
[*] [b]avatars.json[/b] – Stores your uploaded model’s Steam Mod IDs and image paths. Keep it safe to avoid duplicate uploads!
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Important Notice[/h2]

[quote]
By uploading a model, [b]you confirm that you own the rights or license to distribute it[/b].

MateEngine is [u]not responsible[/u] for any unauthorized uploads.

Always respect copyright and licensing terms!
[/quote]

notes.content:
[h1]MateEngine 1.7.0[/h1]

[h3][b][url=https://discord.com/invite/FBKCNWgTDA]Official Discord[/url][/b][/h3]

[h2]NEW FEATURES:[/h2]

You can now add an unlimited number of models (VRM or ME format) by clicking Models → VRM/ME.
Added avatars appear in a list with key details including:

[list]
[*] Thumbnail (if available)

[*] Version

[*] Recommended: 50%
[/list]

Works the same as the spine slider, but for head movement.
[list]
[*] Lets you balance between real-time head tracking and natural animation.

A new toggle allows you to enable or disable hand tracking.
[list]
[*] Enabled by default — uncheck the "Hand Tracking" option to disable it.

Colorful Menus!
Added HUE and SATURATION sliders in the Options menu so you can customize the menu's appearance to your liking.

[*] Improved calculation logic: the pet now moves correctly with window size changes.

[list]
[*] The VRM button is now located under Models → VRM/ME.

  This keeps the interface clean and prepares the layout for future features.
[*] The Settings menu is now fully scrollable.
  Use the scrollbar or drag to scroll.
  Note: Scrolling with the mouse wheel will resize your avatar, not scroll the menu.
* Updated the MateEngine startup sound! Hatsune Miku now greets you with a cute “Mate Engina la la la!”
[/list]


[h2]FIXES:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where clicked buttons would remain visually pressed after release.
[*] Fixed some Memory and CPU related issues to improve performance.
[*] Fixed an issue where windows with scrollbars could be scrolled horizontally, even when it didn’t make sense.
[*] Improved Leg and Feet IK Pass:
  Enhances leg movement in animations for a more natural look and resolves minor visual issues such as "floating" feet or overlapping legs.
[/list]

notes.title: Modding Update 1.6.2
notes.content:
[h1]Changelog 1.6.2 – The Modding Update[/h1]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/K2xriAh.png[/img]

[h3]This update focuses on modding support by introducing MateSDK 1.0.  
You can [url=https://github.com/shinyflvre/Mate-Engine]download[/url] the MateSDK directly from GitHub.[/h3]

Requirements for Developing Mods:  
Unity Hub, Unity 6000.X, and basic knowledge of how to use Unity.

MateSDK / MateEngine 1.6.2 Modding Pipeline  
- Added support for using any shader on models  
- Added support for real-time lights, point lights, and other Unity light sources  
- Added ability to manipulate existing behavior of all controllers  
- Added ability to remove assets, scripts, and features  
- Added support to convert VRM 0.X to .ME file format  
- Added support to convert VRM 1.X to .ME file format  
- Added ability to change clothes of an avatar (.ME only)

Introducing .ME Mods and .ME Models

.ME Models are an evolved variant of VRM files.  
Unlike VRM 0.X or 1.X, .ME is essentially "VRM++" — allowing much more customization.

You can:  
- Use any shaders (e.g., Liltoon, Poiyomi)  
- Add prefabs and other Unity features to your model  
- Create VRChat-style enhancements and features

How to Convert to the .ME File Format

To convert your model to .ME, you'll need a working VRM0 or VRM1 file. Then follow this workflow:

1. Open the MateSDK Unity Project  
2. Import your .vrm file anywhere into the project  
3. Drag the VRM file into the Hierarchy  
4. Modify your VRM however you want – add custom shaders, objects, 3D assets, prefabs  
5. Once finished, open the Model Exporter window  
6. Drag and drop your completed prefab into the exporter  
7. Click Export  
8. Load your custom .ME model

Happy Modding!

notes.title: Custom VRM and Mod Support
notes.content:
[b]We’ve gotten a lot of questions on TikTok about custom VRM models and mod support—so we’d love to take a moment to answer the most common ones![/b]

[b]Many of you asked:[/b]
[i]“Can we mod it?”
“Can I use my own model?”
“My model didn’t work, but it works in another app—can you help?”[/i]

Let’s go through each one:

[h2]Can we mod it?[/h2]

Yes—MateEngine is fully moddable! It’s open source, and the code is available online. You're welcome to create and share your own modifications.

Just one important note: MateEngine uses the AGPL license, which means any modifications you make (that include our source code) must also be shared publicly as open source. This helps keep the community open, transparent, and safe for everyone.

If you're new to this, we recommend reading up on the AGPL license before publishing your mods.

Also, while we fully support modding, we don't use the Steam Workshop for mods due to licensing limitations and review requirements. For example, we can’t legally verify every uploaded VRM file for licensing. Since we’re a small team (just one developer and one musician!), we kindly ask you to use other platforms to share your mods.

[h2]
Can I use my own VRM model?[/h2]

Absolutely! You can load your own custom VRM file as long as it was exported correctly.

Here are a few things to keep in mind:

    VRM 0.x uses MToon shaders

    VRM 1.x uses MToon 1.0 shaders and a strict bone structure
    Example structure:

    Model
    └── Armature
        └── Hips
            └── (Your rig goes here)

If your model follows this format and uses proper shaders, it should load just fine. If you’re unsure how to set up your model, there are great VRM tutorials available on YouTube!

[h2]
My model won’t load, but it works in other apps?[/h2]

If your VRM model doesn’t load in MateEngine, it’s likely due to export issues—such as missing shaders or incorrect bone structures.

You might think:
“But it worked in app X or on website Y?”
That’s totally fair—many apps automatically apply fallback shaders or correct bone structures for you. MateEngine doesn’t do this on purpose: we want creators to be aware of how to properly export and manage their own files.

We know that can be a bit frustrating at first, but it helps everyone learn and create higher-quality content. So before leaving a negative review, please double-check your VRM setup. We’re always happy to point you toward helpful resources!



Thanks so much for your questions and support—we love seeing your creativity and custom characters in MateEngine. Keep exploring, experimenting, and sharing!
